title: Display switcher offers List, Tech View and Board View and marks the active one
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Display Switcher") has two Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17581), led by {Technician-A}, and {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17582), with no lead technician.
  • The Work Orders page shows List at the start: List is the highlighted button in the display switcher.
  • Developer note kept from the automation engineer (nothing for the tester to do): Dev-layer test — fe-unit. Existing coverage: app/src/components/ts/work-orders/**/DisplayOptionSwitcher.spec.ts:42,65,77
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Look at the display switcher at the right of the toolbar and write down which button is highlighted.
  3. Hover the first button of the display switcher and read its tooltip.
  4. Hover the second button and read its tooltip.
  5. Hover the third button and read its tooltip.
  6. Click Tech View in the display switcher.
  7. Look at which switcher button is highlighted.
  8. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  9. Look at which switcher button is highlighted.
  10. Click List in the display switcher.
  11. Look at which switcher button is highlighted.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: the switcher offers exactly three display options, and List is the highlighted one.
  • Steps 3 to 5: the tooltips read List, Tech View and Board View, in that order.
  • Step 7: only Tech View is highlighted.
  • Step 9: only Board View is highlighted.
  • Step 11: only List is highlighted.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 54 (15 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R1, S1-R9 and S1-R9b, read 15 Oct 2026. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 24, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 15 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.19-72f4f3b (staging) on 10/16/2026.

The design's tooltips read Table, By Lead Tech and Board, and this case used to accept any label. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 24) that the tooltips read List, Tech View and Board View; PRD version 54 says so, and a different word is now a fail.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R1: “The Work Orders toolbar offers List, Tech View, and Board View display options.”
  • S1-R9: “The switcher visually indicates the active display option.”
  • S1-R9b: “The switcher’s hover tooltip opens above the switcher, so it never covers the table’s column header row. The tooltips read List, Tech View and Board View.”

AUTOMATION: READY

title: A user who never chose a display sees List
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 2 users · 1 browser · about 15 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • [User-B]: a brand-new user who has never opened Work Orders, with a role that has Work Orders view (e.g. Service Advisor) and this location picked in Location, and an email you can open.
  • Desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • [Tech-A]: one eligible technician at this location. A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Default List" (used by this case only) with one Approved work order [WO-1] led by [Tech-A].
  • Names are examples; what must hold: [User-B] has never opened Work Orders (so has never chosen a display).

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Create everything below in this location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Default List" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Default List": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].
  6. Create a brand-new user who has never opened Work Orders: Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff > New Staff Member with an email you can open (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Never Chose"), a role with Work Orders view (e.g. Service Advisor), at least one Department (required), with this location picked in Location > Save & Close. Accept the invitation and set a password, but do not open Work Orders as this user. Record this user as [User-B].
  7. Check the setup worked: as [User-A], Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Default List" shows [WO-1]; Settings > Staff lists [User-B] at this location. If [User-B] has already opened Work Orders, create another new user and use that one.
custom_steps:
1. Sign out.
  2. Sign in as [User-B].
  3. Open Work Orders from the top navigation.
  4. Look at the work orders area and the display switcher.
  5. Refresh the page.
  6. Look at the display again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The page opens in List: the ordinary work order table, not grouped by technician and not shown as columns of cards.
  • In the display switcher the List option is the highlighted one.
  • After the refresh the page is still in List.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S1-R2, Key Decisions, read 8 Oct 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R2: “List is the default display option for every user until they choose another.”
  • Key Decisions: “Default display option remains List. Existing users see no change until they choose otherwise.”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.

title: Switching display keeps the same tab, search, filters and work orders
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-C} (for example Jenny Wilson) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Fibridge") has exactly three Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17612) led by {Technician-A}, {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17613) led by {Technician-B}, and {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17614) with no lead.
  • Customer {Customer-B} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Fisquare") has one Approved work order, {Work-order-4} (for example S10043-17615), with any lead. {Customer-B}'s name does not contain {Customer-A}'s name, so searching {Customer-A}'s name does not find {Work-order-4}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type the name of {Customer-A}.
  4. Click Status and tick Approved.
  5. Click outside the Status list to close it.
  6. In List, write down every work order number shown.
  7. Click Tech View in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar (tooltip "Tech View").
  8. Write down the work order numbers shown and each group header count.
  9. Click Board View in the display switcher (tooltip "Board View").
  10. Write down the work order numbers on the cards and each column header count.
  11. Click List in the display switcher (tooltip "List").
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 7, 9 and 11: the layout changes straight away on each click, without a page reload.
  • Steps 7 to 11: after every switch the All tab is still selected, the search box still shows the name of {Customer-A}, and Status still shows Approved ticked.
  • Steps 6, 8 and 10: the same work orders appear in all three displays. List shows 3 rows ({Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}), Tech View shows the same 3 (Unassigned 1 + {Technician-A} 1 + {Technician-B} 1 = 3) and Board View shows the same 3 cards. {Work-order-4} appears in none of them.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 52 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R3 and Feature Overview (its filter sentence was reworded in version 52 to name the Technician filter as the second exception, after Imported; this case uses no Technician filter, so the expected results are unchanged), read 14 Oct 2026. Source-verified 14 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R3: “Switching display options immediately re-lays out the current results without changing the filter view, search text, or filters.”
  • Feature Overview: “The existing filter views (the tabs on the left — All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed) and the filter bar (search, status, assigned to me, and so on) apply the same way in every display option.”
  • Feature Overview (the two exceptions): “Imported work orders are one exception: they open in List only (S1-R13a, S1-R13b). The Technician filter is the other: Tech View and Board View offer it and List does not (S1-R15).”

Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Display Follows User" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Display Follows User": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once.     • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].

Add one in Settings > Staff if needed: New Staff Member with an email you can open (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Second Viewer"), a role with Work Orders view, at least one Department (required), this location in Location > Save & Close; accept the invitation and set a password. custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").

  7. Sign out and sign in as [User-B]. Open Work Orders and note the display.

Expected results

  • In the second browser, Work Orders opens in Board View.
  • At the second location, Work Orders opens in Board View.

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S1-R4, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions Confluence 853901313, DR-6 (display option persists across locations).

  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.

Review Decisions 853901313 FF-3 / DR-6. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 30, read 15 Oct 2026. title: Tech View groups work orders under each lead with name, avatar and count
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • Two technicians at this location: [Tech-A] (the expected results call it "Esther Howard") and [Tech-B] (the expected results call it "Ralph Edwards"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Tech Grouping" (used by this case only), with one contact and one asset, so this case's work orders are kept apart from every other work order at the location.
  • Six work orders for that customer: [Tech-A] leads three ([WO-1] Approved, [WO-2] Approved, [WO-3] Estimate); [Tech-B] leads two ([WO-4], [WO-5]); [WO-6] has no lead.
  • What must hold: [Tech-A] leads exactly two Approved and one Estimate work order for this customer. Names and numbers are examples.

Setup

  1. Sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page (you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  2. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm each technician below is active at this location with Time Clock on, or add it: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard); [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards).
  3. Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Tech Grouping" > Save (if it already exists, open it instead). On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, TRK-118) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  4. Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Tech Grouping" and its asset > Save. The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form open: in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; the build offers only ready-made lines), then turn Line Approved on > Save & Close to make it Approved, or leave Line Approved off > Save & Close to keep it an Estimate. Repeat for six work orders in all: [WO-1] and [WO-2] Approved, [WO-3] an Estimate, [WO-4], [WO-5] and [WO-6] Approved. Record each number shown (the expected results call [WO-1] "S1-702", [WO-2] "S1-644" and [WO-3] "S1-455") (numbers on this site look like "S10043-17581").
  5. Set the leads: on an Approved work order pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned. Here: [WO-1], [WO-2] and [WO-3] = [Tech-A]; [WO-4] and [WO-5] = [Tech-B]; [WO-6] no lead.
  6. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search ZZAUTOTEST F2 Tech Grouping — six work orders show; in List, Lead Technician reads [Tech-A] on [WO-1] to [WO-3], [Tech-B] on [WO-4] and [WO-5], and nothing on [WO-6]; [WO-3] has status Estimate. If not, fix the lead or status before starting.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type ZZAUTOTEST F2 Tech Grouping so only this test's work orders show.
  4. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (tooltip "Tech View").
  5. Look at how the table is divided.
  6. Read the header of [Tech-A]'s group: name, picture or initials, and number.
  7. Count the rows under [Tech-A].
  8. Open the Status filter, tick Approved only and close it.
  9. Read [Tech-A]'s header number and count her rows again.

Expected results

  • The number equals the rows listed under it. Example: Esther Howard shows 3 with 3 rows (S1-702, S1-644, S1-455), Ralph Edwards shows 2 with 2 rows.
  • After filtering to Approved, Esther Howard's number becomes 2 and 2 rows are listed (S1-702, S1-644): 3 - 1 Estimate = 2.

custom_steps:

  12. Click the Column Selection button.
  13. Turn Assigned Techs off.
  14. Close the menu and read the Tech View column headers.
  15. Click the Column Selection button, turn Assigned Techs on and close the menu.
  16. Read the Tech View column headers.
  17. Click the Column Selection button and try to turn off Status, then Number, then Customer.
  18. Turn Unit off.
  19. Close the menu and read the Tech View column headers.
  20. Click the Column Selection button, turn Unit on and close the menu.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: List's menu does not offer Assigned Techs.
  • Steps 6 and 7: Tech View has its own Column Selection button, which opens Tech View's own column menu.
  • Step 7: every column offered in List's menu is also offered in Tech View's menu, and Tech View's menu also offers Assigned Techs, which is on.
  • Step 11: On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician each show as a column in the Tech View table.
  • Step 14: the Assigned Techs column no longer shows in Tech View.
  • Step 16: the Assigned Techs column shows in Tech View again.

The earlier note that the design's Tech View menu leaves out some List columns is removed: version 51 keeps every List column available in Tech View, with On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician off by default. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answers 14 and 25, read 15 Oct 2026. title: A group's work orders made with their lead follow List's default order
refs: SV-10052 (S9-R14 created with lead keeps initial sort / S2-R6 / S9-R3 - spec v64)
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and Schedule access, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • User {User-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Sort Viewer) is a staff member with the Admin role at {Location-A}, can sign in, and has never changed or saved a sort in List.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Owen Created QA1019) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User, so they have a row on the Schedule page. {Technician-A} leads no work order.
  • Customers {Customer-A} (for example "Alpha Freight QA1019"), {Customer-B} (for example "Mid Trucking QA1019") and {Customer-C} (for example "Zeta Hauling QA1019") start with different first letters, end with the same words (for example QA1019) and each has an asset.
  • Nobody has reordered {Technician-A}'s work orders at {Location-A}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice, Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Click Schedule in the top menu and find {Technician-A}'s row.
  2. Click an empty cell in {Technician-A}'s row. A small menu opens with Assign Work Order, Create Event and New Work Order. Click New Work Order.
  3. In the New Work Order dialog choose {Customer-C} in Customer, choose its asset in Asset and click Save. Write down the new work order's number ({Work-order-1}).
  4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for {Customer-A} ({Work-order-2}), then for {Customer-B} ({Work-order-3}), then for {Customer-B} again ({Work-order-4}). Use an empty cell each time. The four work orders are now made in this order: {Customer-C}, {Customer-A}, {Customer-B}, {Customer-B}.
  5. Sign in as {User-B}. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click List in the display switcher.
  6. Type the shared end of the three customer names (for example QA1019) in Search.
  7. Write down the order of the four work orders in List, and the name in their Lead Technician column.
  8. Click Tech View in the display switcher and write down the order of the rows in {Technician-A}'s group.
  9. Click Board View in the display switcher and write down the order of the cards in {Technician-A}'s column.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 7: all four work orders show {Technician-A} as Lead Technician, because each was made with its lead. List shows them in its usual default order: by customer name from A to Z, and the two {Customer-B} work orders newest first: {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-4}, {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-1}.
  • Step 8: Tech View's rows in {Technician-A}'s group are in that same order: {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-4}, {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-1}. They are NOT in the order they were made, and they did NOT go to the bottom one after another (S9-R14).
  • Step 9: Board View's cards in {Technician-A}'s column are in the same order as Tech View's rows.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

  • Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View) and SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder). PRD “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, Confluence 845185030, version 64, S9-R14, S2-R6 and S9-R3, read 19 Oct 2026.
  • Chris Ward on the PRD (v53), quoted on SV-11312 (comment 78792, 15 Oct 2026): “A work order created with its lead keeps the initial sort.”
  • Companion case C96929 covers the other half of the same rule: a work order that gets its lead after it was made goes to the bottom.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R14: “… Going to the bottom applies only to work moved onto a technician. A work order created or split off with a lead keeps the initial sort (S9-R3).”
  • S2-R6: “Before a manual order is saved, use the List’s default work order sort, ties included, exactly as the List sorts today: work orders for the same customer go by start date, newest first. The List itself does not change.”

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-10043 and the Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options specification version 64 (S9-R14, S2-R6, S9-R3). Last checked against build v26.40.19-e435950 (staging) on 10/19/2026.

  • S3-R13: “Reveal the card’s more-actions overlay on hover or keyboard focus.”

Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or the first one when none has been (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”

title: Pinned technician columns after deactivation or removal from this location
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}, in a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. The company has a second location, {Location-B}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • A second user, {User-B}, whose role has Work orders > View only, is signed in at {Location-A} in a second browser or a private window.
    For example: {User-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C368131 Viewer.
  • Three active technicians work at {Location-A}: {Technician-A}, and {Technician-B} and {Technician-C}, who are made for this case only. {Technician-B} leads no work order.
    For example: {Technician-A} is Esther Howard, {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Jenny Pinned and {Technician-C} is ZZAUTOTEST Theresa Pinned.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has two Approved work orders, with no shift booked for them on the Schedule: {Work-order-1} led by {Technician-A}, and {Work-order-2} led by {Technician-C}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C368131 Pinned Gone, {Work-order-1} is S10043-17691 and {Work-order-2} is S10043-17692.
  • You and {User-B} both have {Technician-B} and {Technician-C} pinned in Board View.
  • Starting screen: the Work Orders page with no filter set (nothing ticked in "Status", no choice in "Asset on Site", "Assigned to me" off, "Search" empty).
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Go to your initials (top right) > "Settings" > "Staff".
  2. Deactivate {Technician-B}: click the edit icon on {Technician-B}, click "Deactivate Account" and confirm.
  3. Move {Technician-C} to {Location-B}: click the edit icon on {Technician-C}, change "Location" to {Location-B} and click "Save & Close"; then click the "Department(s)" button on her row, click the bin icon next to {Location-A} and close the window (the Location field alone leaves her at {Location-A}).
  4. Click "Work Orders" in the top menu.
  5. Click the "All" tab and type the name of {Customer-A} in "Search".
  6. Click "Board View" in the display switcher.
  7. Look at the pinned columns right after "Unassigned".
  8. Find {Technician-C}'s column further along and look at its header.
  9. Drag {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  10. Drag {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-C}'s column and let go.
  11. Read the message that appears and check where {Work-order-1} is.
  12. Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-C}'s column onto the "Unassigned" column and let go.
  13. Check which column {Work-order-2} is in and whether {Technician-C} still has a column.
  14. In the second browser, as {User-B}, go to "Work Orders" > "All" > "Board View".
  15. Look at the pinned columns right after "Unassigned".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 7: {Technician-B}'s column is still shown right after Unassigned, so the pin is kept. It is marked inactive and empty, and it reads "No work orders", not "Drag a work order here to assign it".
  • Step 7: {Technician-C} is not among the pinned columns.
  • Step 8: {Technician-C}'s column appears further along as a normal column holding {Work-order-2}, with no pin icon and no inactive marker.
  • Step 9: the card cannot be dropped on {Technician-B}'s column. {Work-order-1} stays in {Technician-A}'s column.
  • Steps 10 and 11: the drop is refused with the message "This technician can't be assigned work orders." and {Work-order-1} stays in {Technician-A}'s column.
  • Step 13: {Work-order-2} is in Unassigned and {Technician-C} no longer has a column at all.
  • Step 15: for the view-only {User-B}, {Technician-B}'s column also reads "No work orders", and there is no {Technician-C} column.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician) and SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 49 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S3-R20a, S3-E3, S3-N4, S3-R20b and its context note (Sasha Grosman's answer to SQ-11, 24 Sep 2026), S3-R20c (added in version 49) and S4-N5 (widened in version 49), both from Chris Ward's answer 2 of 14 Oct 2026 to our question sheet; read 14 Oct 2026. Sasha Grosman's answer to engineering of 24 Sep 2026 treated a technician who is no longer at this location like an inactive one; PRD version 49 (14 Oct 2026) says that column shows no inactive marker and refuses drops with its own message, and we take the later PRD as prevailing. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version, updated 9 Oct 2026 for PRD v44, was not re-run on the QA build).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R20a: “The empty column of a pinned technician who has been deactivated shows “No work orders” to every user, because nothing can be dropped there (S4-N5).”
  • S3-E3: “Retain a technician’s pin after deactivation.”
  • S3-N4: “Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.”
  • S3-R20b: “A pinned technician who is not enrolled at this location gets no column here. If they still lead work orders at this location, they appear as a normal, unpinned column holding that work.”
  • S3-R20c: “The column of S3-R20b takes no drops. Dropping a work order on it is refused with "This technician can't be assigned work orders." and the work order stays where it was. The column shows no inactive marker, because the technician is not deactivated (S3-N4). Once it holds no work orders, the column is no longer shown.”
  • S4-N5: “Nothing can be dropped onto the column/group of an inactive technician (S2-N2, S3-N2) or of a technician who is not enrolled at this location (S3-R20c).”
  • Context note (S3-R20a, S3-R20b): “A pin only counts at locations where the technician is enrolled.”

Last checked against build v26.40.17-ddb9ba1 (staging) on 10/14/2026.

custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 10 minutes · no setup

custom_steps:
1. Click Work Orders in the top menu, then the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  2. At the right of the toolbar, click Board View (the right-most of the three view buttons, tooltip "Board View").
  3. Look at the scroll bar at the very bottom of the board, under the technician columns.
  4. Scroll down inside the Unassigned column and look at the thin scroll bar that shows inside that column.
  5. Compare the grey handle on the bottom bar with the width of one technician column.
  6. Drag the grey handle all the way to the right, then all the way back to the left.
  7. Make the browser window narrower (about the width of a small laptop) and look at the handle again. Then change to a location with only a few technicians and look at the handle again.
  8. Click your initials at the top right > Dark, look at the bottom bar again, then switch back to Light.
  9. Click Tech View (middle view button), then List (left view button), and look at their scroll bars.

Expected results

  • The bottom bar is clearly thicker than the thin scroll bar inside a column.
  • The grey handle is at least about half as wide as one technician column, at every window size.
  • On a location with only a few technicians the handle is longer than on a big board. How much longer depends on the window width: on a wide window it is much longer, on a narrow one only a little. That is correct; it is never shorter than about half a column.
  • Dragging right reaches the last technician; dragging left comes back to the first one. Unassigned stays in place on the left the whole time.
  • In Dark the bar and its handle are still easy to see.
  • Tech View and List keep their usual thin scroll bars; nothing changed there.
  • In Firefox the bottom bar looks like Firefox's normal scroll bar. That is correct.

A technician column is about 290 px wide, so half a column is about 150 px. The bar inside a column is about 10 px; the bottom bar is 16 px.

custom_preconds:
Preconditions

Each of them can sign in (each staff record has an email and an accepted invite). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Notifications" (used by this case only) with one Approved work order [WO-1] led by [Tech-A].
  • A second browser (or a private window) for signing in as the technicians.
  • Names and the number are examples; what must hold: all three technicians can sign in and see their notifications.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard), [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards), [Tech-C] (e.g. Dana Ortiz). Give each an email you can open, accept the invite and set a password, so [Tech-A], [Tech-B] and [Tech-C] can sign in.
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Notifications" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Notifications": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].
  6. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Notifications" shows [WO-1] with Lead Technician [Tech-A]; in the second browser you can sign in as each of the three technicians. If not, fix the lead or finish the missing invite before starting; then clear the search.
custom_steps:
1. Open [WO-1]'s work order page and change Lead Technician from [Tech-A] to [Tech-B] there.
  2. In a second browser, sign in as [Tech-A] and then as [Tech-B], and write down any notification each of them received for this change (notification bell, email, or none).
  3. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  4. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Lead Notifications" in Search.
  5. In the first browser, drag the card from [Tech-B]'s column into [Tech-C]'s column.
  6. If a "Clear …'s scheduled shifts?" prompt opens, click Keep shifts.
  7. In the second browser, sign in as [Tech-B] and then as [Tech-C] and write down any notification each received.
  8. Repeat steps 3 to 7 in Tech View with the row's More actions > Reassign lead technician, moving it back to [Tech-A].
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A lead change made in Board View or Tech View produces exactly the same notifications as a lead change made on the work order page (step 2 compared with steps 6 and 8). The product owner records that no notification is sent on a lead change today, so none is expected in either place.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

custom_steps:

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 49 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R11, S4-R22, S4-R23, S4-R24, S4-R28 (reworded in version 49 on 14 Oct 2026 from Chris Ward's answer 1 of 14 Oct 2026: a work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line, judged at the moment the lead changes; first defined in version 47 after SV-11126) and S4-R29, read 14 Oct 2026. Review Decisions DR-31 (optional whole-work-order shift clearing). Schedule shift window labels "Entire work order" / "Choose lines" from the Schedule suite. Each work order has two lines so that the 13:00–15:00 shift covers only some of them. On a one-line work order a shift on that line counts (version 49, S4-R28). Source-verified 14 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R11: “When changing the lead technician in Board View or Tech View, ask whether to clear the outgoing lead’s work-order-level scheduled shifts.”
  • S4-R29: “The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.”
  • S4-R22: “If the user chooses to clear shifts, remove only the outgoing lead’s shifts scheduled against that whole work order.”
  • S4-R23: “If the user chooses to keep shifts, change the lead technician and retain the existing shifts.”
  • S4-R24: “Never clear shifts scheduled against individual work order lines through this prompt.”
  • S4-R28: “The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line of the work order, judged at the moment the lead changes; this is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. Lines not yet approved, and declined lines, are ignored. On a work order with one line, a shift on that line counts, and so does a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line. A shift on only some approved lines does not show the prompt, and that includes an Entire work order shift once a line has been added and approved after it was made.”

Setup

  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] = "Esther Howard" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it), [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards), [Tech-C] (e.g. Dana Ortiz). Give [Tech-A] an email you can open, accept the invite and set a password, so [Tech-A] can sign in.
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Status And Time Kept" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Status And Time Kept": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close.   10. Check the setup worked: [WO-1] reads In Progress with Lead Technician [Tech-A] and [Tech-A]'s clock running; the Schedule shows [Tech-A]'s 8:00–12:00 shift on it tomorrow; you have written down Actual hours and Total Hours. If not, redo the missing step before starting.

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R19, S4-R20, S4-R21, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions DR-18 / DR-31. Source-verified 8 October 2026.

Preconditions

  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011). A desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • [User-A]: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • A second location [Loc-2] you can switch to (your initials at the top right > Change Location) (e.g. "Staging Lethbridge - 4310"); your user is enrolled at both.
  • One technician at this location: [Tech-A] (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Board Fields Saved" (used by this case only), with one contact and one asset, so this case's work orders are kept apart from every other work order at the location. The asset has a VIN (e.g. "1FD0W5HY2EEA05499").
  • One Approved work order for that customer, [WO-1], led by [Tech-A].
  • A second browser or computer is available. Board View's Column Selection starts with Customer on and VIN/serial off (turn them back if needed).

Setup

  1. Sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page (you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  2. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff > New Staff Member, enter First Name and Last Name (e.g. "Esther Howard") and an email. Pick a Role that is not Office User or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), pick at least one Department (required), set Location to this location and turn Time Clock on, then click Save & Close. Record as [Tech-A].
  3. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Board Fields Saved" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then VIN/Serial # (e.g. "1FD0W5HY2EEA05499"), Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  4. Create the work order: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Board Fields Saved" and its Asset > Save, and record its number as [WO-1] (e.g. "S1-702"). The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close.
  5. Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page and choose [Tech-A] (e.g. "Esther Howard"). (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.)
  6. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search ZZAUTOTEST F2 Board Fields Saved > Board View — the [WO-1] card shows the customer and Lead technician [Tech-A] and no VIN. If Customer is off or VIN/serial is on in Column Selection, set them back before starting.

  6. Read the [WO-1] card.
  7. Log out, log back in and open Board View.

  9. Switch to [Loc-2] and open Board View.

custom_steps:

custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011). A desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • [User-A]: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • [User-B] = "Nate Nofinance" (the expected results name him, so keep this name): a second user whose role is a custom role with Work Orders view and, for now, See Financial Data, signed in in a second browser.
  • One technician at this location: [Tech-A] (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 No Dollar Amounts" (used by this case only), with one contact and one asset, so this case's work orders are kept apart from every other work order at the location.
  • One Approved work order for that customer, [WO-1], led by [Tech-A], with a price.
  • As Nate Nofinance, Total price is on in Tech View's Column Selection menu and in Board View's Column Selection.

Setup

  1. Sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page (you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  2. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff > New Staff Member, enter First Name and Last Name (e.g. "Esther Howard") and an email. Pick a Role that is not Office User or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), pick at least one Department (required), set Location to this location and turn Time Clock on, then click Save & Close. Record as [Tech-A].
  3. Settings > Roles & Permissions > Create Custom Role (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Finance Toggle") > turn on Work Orders view and See Financial Data > Save.
  4. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff > New Staff Member for "Nate Nofinance" with an email you can open, Role = the new custom role, at least one Department (required), with this location picked in Location, Time Clock off > Save & Close, then accept the invitation and set a password. Keep him signed in in a second browser.
  5. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name "ZZAUTOTEST F2 No Dollar Amounts" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  6. Create the work order: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 No Dollar Amounts" and its Asset > Save, and record its number as [WO-1] (e.g. "S1-702"). The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close.
  7. Set the leads: on an Approved work order pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned. Here: [WO-1] = [Tech-A].
  8. As Nate Nofinance, turn Total price on in Tech View's Column Selection menu and in Board View's Column Selection.
  9. Check the setup worked: as Nate Nofinance, Work Orders > All tab > Search ZZAUTOTEST F2 No Dollar Amounts — Tech View shows a Total price column and the Board View card shows a dollar amount. If not, check his role has See Financial Data on.
custom_steps:
1. As the admin, edit Nate Nofinance's role and turn See Financial Data off, then save.
  2. As Nate Nofinance sign in again, open Work Orders, pick Tech View and search for ZZAUTOTEST F2 No Dollar Amounts.
  3. Read the columns and open Column Selection.
  4. Open every filter in the toolbar and read its options.
  5. Pick Board View, read the card and open Column Selection.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Tech View has no Total price column and its column chooser does not offer it; Board View cards show no dollar amount and Fields to display does not offer total price.
  • No filter offers a dollar-amount option, and Nate's earlier saved choice (Total price on) does not bring any dollar value back. List is not part of this change and stays as in production.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10048 (Story 5, Fields to display (Board View) and columns (Tech View)); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S5-E2, S5-E6, read 8 Oct 2026. custom_steps:

  2. Look at the size of the text in {Work-order-1}'s row, of the column header labels and of the percentage beside the progress bar.
  3. Click the density button and choose "Compact".
  4. Compare the same texts with what you saw at step 2.
  5. Click the density button and choose "Comfortable".
  6. Compare the same texts with what you saw at step 2.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: "Regular" is in use.
  • Step 2: the row text is the normal size (14 px). The column header labels and the percentage are smaller (12 px).
  • Step 3: "Compact" is in use and the rows are tighter.
  • Step 4: at Compact the row text is the same size as at Regular (14 px), not smaller. The column header labels and the percentage keep their own smaller size (12 px), the same as at Regular.

  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Scheduled Techs Lines" (used by this case only), with one contact and one asset.

  • The work order number and line names are examples.

Setup

  1. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm each technician below exists and is eligible, or add them with New Staff Member: First Name and Last Name ("Jenny Wilson", "Ralph Edwards", "Dana Ortiz") and an email; a Role that is not Office User or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"); at least one Department (required); Location = this location; Time Clock on > Save & Close.
  2. Top menu Customers > New Customer, Name "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Scheduled Techs Lines" > Save (skip if it already exists). title: Nothing can be dropped on an inactive technician, and a failed drop goes back
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST C97010 Failed Drop") is used by this case only.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17701) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
  • Work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17702) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}, is Complete (reviewed) and has not been invoiced, so Create Invoice is offered on its Finance tab.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17703) for {Customer-A} is led by technician {Technician-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dan Delta), made for this case only.
  • After {Work-order-3} was given its lead, {Technician-C}'s staff account was deactivated.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} or {Work-order-3}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Read {Technician-C}'s column header and its count.
  4. Drag {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-C}'s column and let go.
  5. Read where {Work-order-1} is and {Technician-C}'s count.
  6. Open a second browser tab and open {Work-order-2} in it.
  7. In the second tab, click the Finance tab and click Create Invoice.
  8. Go back to the first tab. Do not refresh it.
  9. Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  10. Read where {Work-order-2} is and the alert that appears.
  11. Wait about ten seconds and check whether the alert is still shown.
  12. Click the alert's dismiss (X) button.
  13. Refresh the page.
  14. Open {Work-order-2} and read its Lead Technician.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: {Technician-C}'s column is still shown with {Work-order-3}, is marked inactive and its count is 1.
  • Step 5: the drop is not accepted. {Work-order-1} stays in {Technician-A}'s column, {Technician-C}'s count stays 1 and no message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-C}" appears.
  • Steps 9 and 10: the move cannot be saved. {Work-order-2} goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and the alert reads "Failed to update lead technician, please try again.", with a message explaining that the work order's status does not allow the change. If the first tab already showed {Work-order-2} as locked and it could not be dragged onto {Technician-B}'s column, this part cannot be checked by hand: write "not checked by hand" in the result comment.
  • Steps 11 and 12: the alert stays on screen until you dismiss it.
  • Steps 13 and 14: {Work-order-2} is in {Technician-A}'s column and its Lead Technician is still {Technician-A}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns), SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician) and SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-N2, S9-E1, S4-N5 (widened in version 49 from Chris Ward's answer 2 of 14 Oct 2026 to also name a technician not enrolled at this location; this case checks the inactive technician), S3-N2, S3-N4, S4-E3, S4-N3, S4-N8, S4-N2, S4-R10 and S4-R5, read 19 Oct 2026. In versions 66 to 68 (19 Oct 2026) the message after a lead change became "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo; step 5 checks that it does not appear. The failed save is produced by invoicing the work order in a second tab before the drop lands, which replaces the earlier way of turning the network off. Source-verified 19 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-N2: “Keep matching work visible in its deactivated technician’s column.”
  • S3-N4: “Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.”
  • S4-N5: “Nothing can be dropped onto the column/group of an inactive technician (S2-N2, S3-N2) or of a technician who is not enrolled at this location (S3-R20c).”
  • S9-N2: “Apply S4-N5’s inactive-destination restriction and S4-N3/S4-N8’s failure recovery to drag reassignment.”
  • S9-E1: “If status or permission changes before a drop completes, revalidate and reject unauthorized reassignment under S4-E3/S4-N3.”
  • S4-E3: “If status becomes prohibited during a drag, reject the drop using S4-N3 and S4-N8, with a status explanation.”
  • S4-N3: “If reassignment fails, return the card or row to its original column or group.”
  • S4-N8: “Failed reassignment shows a user-dismissible alert: “Failed to update lead technician, please try again.””
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Invoiced or Paid status. An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Declined and Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today.”
  • S4-R10: “Enforce the prohibited-status rule in S4-N2 on every lead-change path, including requests that bypass interface controls.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”

title: A work order created with a lead keeps its normal place, not the bottom
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customers {Customer-A}, {Customer-B} and {Customer-C} are used by this case only, their names start with the same words (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Created With Lead") and end, in name order, with Bravo Co, Charlie Co and Delta Co.
  • Approved work orders {Work-order-1} (for {Customer-A}) and {Work-order-2} (for {Customer-C}) (for example S10043-17741 and S10043-17742) are led by {Technician-A}. {Customer-B} has no work order yet; the one created in step 5 is {Work-order-3}.
  • Nobody has reordered {Technician-A}'s work at {Location-A}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the shared start of the customer names (for example ZZAUTOTEST F3 Created With Lead) in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Read {Technician-A}'s column.
  5. Click Create Work Order, pick {Customer-B} and its asset, choose {Technician-A} as Lead Technician in that window and create it. If the New Work Order window has no Lead Technician field, split a line of {Work-order-1} off into a new work order instead (it keeps {Technician-A} as lead) and write down which way you used. The new work order is {Work-order-3}.
  6. Go back to Work Orders > All > Board View with the same search and read {Technician-A}'s column.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: {Technician-A}'s column reads {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}.
  • Step 6: {Work-order-3} sits in its customer-name place: {Technician-A}'s column reads {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-2}, and {Work-order-3} is not at the bottom. If you used Split, the split-off work order also takes its customer-name place, not the bottom.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-R14, S9-R3 and S2-R6, read 19 Oct 2026. In version 53 (15 Oct 2026) S2-R6 was reworded to spell out the List's tie-break; the expected results are unchanged. Engineering question and plan: PRD footer comment by Slavcho Mitrov, 29 Sep 2026, answered in the 7 Oct PRD. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R14: “A work order that gets a new lead from the lead technician dialog (Assign or Reassign lead technician) or from its detail page goes to the bottom of the new technician’s work, for everyone at the location, in both views. A work order dragged to a technician goes where it is dropped. Removing the lead with the menu’s Unassign action (S11-R9) or on the detail page puts the work order in Unassigned in the initial sort, not at the bottom, so it is not lost behind every other unassigned work order. Going to the bottom applies only to work moved onto a technician. A work order created or split off with a lead keeps the initial sort (S9-R3).”
  • S9-R3: “Once anyone at the location has reordered a technician’s work orders, use that saved order instead of the initial sort. Once a user has reordered technician groups/columns, use their saved order instead of the initial technician sort.”
  • S2-R6: “Before a manual order is saved, use the List’s default work order sort, ties included, exactly as the List sorts today: work orders for the same customer go by start date, newest first. The List itself does not change. A work order that gets a new lead after it was created goes to the bottom of that technician’s work instead (S9-R14).”

Until 15 Oct 2026 Story 11 only listed keyboard behaviour the design still had to define, so this case asked the tester to try keys and write down what each did. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 28): Tab reaches every control, Enter opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the control that opened a menu or dialog, reassigning by keyboard goes through the ⋯ menu, and there is no keyboard drag. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
  • S11-R4: “Enter on a focused row or card opens the work order, the same as a click.”
  • S11-R10: “Opening a work order by keyboard is Enter (S11-R4); dragging is by mouse or touch only, so the two never conflict. A mouse click without a drag opens the work order as today (S2-R8).”
  • S11-R9: “Assigning, reassigning and unassigning by keyboard go through the more-actions menu: Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician (S3-R14) opens the lead technician dialog, and Unassign is a menu item. There is no keyboard drag in this release, so reordering work orders and technicians is by mouse or touch only.”

title: Field selection rate is one combined share across all users, not an average
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: about 30 minutes, over two different days of the same week (Monday to Sunday).
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide; Admin sign-in for the setup (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button).
  • Work in one location throughout, shown next to the bell in the top bar (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials (top right) > Change Location. Create everything in that location.
  • No Google Analytics access is needed: you read what the page sends in the browser's developer tools (Chrome or Edge). Press F12 > Network tab > tick Preserve log > type collect in the filter box. Click a collect request > Payload tab. Each event lists en (event name), ep.element_location (list, tech_view or board_view), ep.element_label (the field or density), ep.setting_value (on or off), ep.setting_source (default = never changed, saved = chosen earlier) and uid (the user). One request can hold several events, one per line.
  • Turn off any ad blocker for this site, and use a new private window for each user so their messages are not stopped or mixed up.
  • Board View starts every new user with VIN/Serial off and Total price on.

Setup

  1. Settings > Roles & Permissions: create a role with Work Orders View but without See financial data (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST No Money").
  2. Settings > Staff > New Staff Member: four new users at this location (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Rate U1" to "U4"); finish each invite so they can sign in. U1, U2 and U3 get a role with Work Orders View and See financial data; U4 gets the role from step 1.
  3. Check: as U4, Board View > Column Selection does not offer Total price.
custom_steps:
1. For each user below use a new private window with the browser tools open as described in the Preconditions (F12 > Network > Preserve log > filter collect). After each user, write down from the collect requests their uid, every work_orders_field_load event for vin and total_price (with ep.setting_value), and every work_orders_field_toggle event (ep.element_label and ep.setting_value). Then sign out and close the window.
  2. Day 1: sign in as U1, open Work Orders > Board View > Column Selection, and turn VIN/Serial on, off, then on again.
  3. Day 2 (a different calendar day): sign in as U2, open Board View and turn VIN/Serial on.
  4. Day 2: sign in as U3, open Board View and turn Total price off.
  5. Day 2: sign in as U4 and open Board View. Change nothing.
  6. Work out the week's figures from your notes, counting each user (uid) once. For each field: the users exposed to it are those with a work_orders_field_load event for it; the users selecting it are those whose last value for it (the load, then any toggles after it) is on. Rate = users selecting ÷ users exposed, over the whole week, not per day.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • VIN/Serial: 4 users saw it (U1 to U4) and 2 have it on (U1, U2), so the rate is 2 ÷ 4 = 50%. U1 counts once however many times they toggled.
  • The figure must not be the average of daily rates. Day 1 = 1 ÷ 1 = 100% and day 2 = 1 ÷ 3 = 33.3%, so their average of 66.7% would be wrong. The correct figure is 50%.
  • Total price: only U1, U2 and U3 could see it (U4 has no financial data, so U4 has no total_price field_load event). U1 and U2 have it on (default) and U3 turned it off, so the rate is 2 ÷ 3 = 66.7%, not 2 ÷ 4 = 50%.
  • Each user keeps the same uid on every event, on both days.
  • The report page itself is built by the report owner inside Google Analytics, outside ShopView, and is not part of this test (QA lead's decision below).

title: A refused lead change in Edit Work Order saves none of the other edits
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 15 minutes.

  • One work order [WO-1] with status Complete (reviewed, not invoiced), led by [Tech-A], Mileage 120,000, Engine Hours 3,420, Customer PO "PO-100".
  • Names and numbers are examples, except names the expected results quote, which must be used exactly.

Setup

  1. Technicians: your initials (top right) > Settings > Staff. A person counts as a technician only if Active, Time Clock on, Role not Office User or Time Clock User, and this location in Location. To add one: New Staff Member > First Name, Last Name, Email, Role "Technician", one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. You need: two, [Tech-A] and [Tech-B].
  2. Customer: Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST Edit WO Refused" > Save. On its Contacts tab > New Contact > First and Last Name > Save. On its Assets tab > New Asset > pick the contact, Year, Make (required), Model, Unit "TRK-118" > Save.
  3. Work order: Work Orders > Create Work Order > Customer "ZZAUTOTEST Edit WO Refused" > its asset > Save (if a credit-limit Confirmation appears, click Create). In New Line > "What Are You Doing?" type "grease" and pick "Service - Full grease service" (no parts) > Line Approved on > Save & Close. Write down the number (top left) as [WO-1] ("S1-714" in the expected results).
  4. On [WO-1], in the card at the left, pick [Tech-A] in Lead Technician (it saves at once; it can only be changed once the work order is Approved).
  5. In the same card type Mileage 120000 and Engine Hours 3420 (each saves when you leave the field). On the Finance tab type "PO-100" in Customer PO.
  6. Bring [WO-1] to Complete: Lines tab > Complete on the line > type any Tech Story (if "Missing Details" shows, fill it, e.g. a Mileage) > Complete Line; the status reads Review. Click Mark Reviewed (if asked for a VIN, type any 17 characters, e.g. 1FVACWDT1BDAZ0001) > Confirm Review; the status reads Complete.
  7. Check: reload [WO-1]. Status Complete, Lead Technician [Tech-A], Mileage 120,000, Engine Hours 3,420, Customer PO "PO-100".

1. Open [WO-1] (Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST Edit WO Refused" > click the work order). Its status reads Complete.
  2. Click the Finance tab and click Create Invoice so the work order is Invoiced. A New Customer Payment window opens: leave it open and do not pay (do not close it with its X, which takes the invoice back off; QA lead decision 23 Oct 2026).
  3. Reload the page. The status reads Invoiced.
  4. There is no separate Edit Work Order window; the edits are tried on the status card (the card at the left of the work order page that shows the status, Lead Technician, Mileage and Engine Hours).
  5. On the status card try to change Lead Technician to [Tech-B].
  6. Try to change Mileage to 120500.
  7. Try to change Engine Hours to 3470.
  8. Reload the page and read Lead Technician, Mileage and Engine Hours on the status card.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 5 to 7: none of the three can be changed on an Invoiced work order. Lead Technician offers no list of technicians to pick from, and Mileage and Engine Hours cannot be edited (or, if a change is tried, it is refused with a message and not saved).
  • Step 8: Lead Technician still reads "Esther Howard", Mileage 120,000 and Engine Hours 3,420. None of the edits was saved.
  • Note: the Customer PO on the Finance tab has its own separate save and is not part of this check (QA lead's decision below).

Source — where this behaviour comes from

  • QA lead decision, 9 Oct 2026: there is no separate Edit Work Order window for an existing work order; the lead technician, mileage and engine hours are changed on the card at the left of the work order page.
  • QA lead decision, 12 Oct 2026: on an invoiced work order the lead, mileage and engine hours cannot be changed and stay as they were, which passes; the Customer PO is saved separately on the Finance tab and is not part of this check.

  • QA handoff §7: “Edit Work Order on a Paid work order, with a different lead and a changed mileage, is refused”

title: A line with labor by a deleted staff member still reads Deleted user
custom_preconds:
Purpose

Verify the existing regression expectation that scheduling another technician on a line does not replace its “Deleted user” labor attribution.

Preconditions

  1. Use the environment and build being tested. Sign in as an Owner/Admin or a user with access to view work orders and create Schedule shifts.
  2. Select one location and keep it selected throughout the test.
  3. Have an existing work order [WO-1] with a line [Line-1] whose recorded labor belongs to a since-deleted staff member. Its Labor row must already read “Deleted user”.
  4. Have an active technician [Tech-J] available for scheduling at the same location.
  5. The work order and line must allow a line-specific Schedule shift to be created.
custom_steps:
1. Open [WO-1] → Lines and identify [Line-1]. Confirm that its Labor row reads “Deleted user” before changing anything.
  2. Open Schedule at the same location and select a suitable future date. Find [WO-1], drag it onto [Tech-J]’s row at an available time, and open the shift-creation dialog.
  3. Choose lines, select only [Line-1], set the duration to 2 hours, and create the shift.
  4. Confirm that the new shift is shown for [Tech-J] on [Line-1].
  5. Reopen [WO-1] → Lines, refresh if needed, and read [Line-1]’s Labor row.
custom_expected:
Step 1: [Line-1] displays “Deleted user” and has recorded labor attributed to a since-deleted staff member. If this starting data is absent, stop and record the missing fixture.

Step 2: The shift-creation dialog opens for the correct work order, technician, location and date.

Step 3: A 2-hour shift is created for [Tech-J] on [Line-1] only.

Step 4: The Schedule shows the shift on the selected line under [Tech-J].

Step 5: The Labor row still reads “Deleted user”; the scheduled technician does not replace the recorded labor attribution.

Source basis — distinguish the requirement from the blocker

PRD: Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options, version 58, checked 16 October 2026: S7-R8 applies when a line has no labor technician and has scheduled technicians; S7-R10 covers a line with neither. Neither requirement explicitly mentions “Deleted user”, requires deletion of staff with logged labor, or defines the staff-deletion rules. These requirements provide context, not the explicit “Deleted user” expectation.

The explicit expected result in Step 5 is retained from the original case’s cited developer regression list (received 8 October 2026) and QA handoff test plan (generated 8 October 2026), §8. Original quoted handoff wording: “A line with real labor keeps its labor technician, and "Deleted user" stays.” The underlying regression list and handoff document were not independently retrieved during this review; this attribution comes from the existing case.

PR #3548 and SV-9769 confirm the scheduled-technician fallback context. The PR also recognizes historical records naming since-deleted technicians. This supports retaining the historical-data regression check, but does not add a requirement that deleting staff with logged labor must be allowed.

The Blocked result comes from the 15 October execution’s reported inability to obtain the required data on staging. It is not a PRD-mandated block, and it is not evidence that the “Deleted user” behavior failed. Re-run when a qualifying fixture is available; no blanket automation hold is imposed by this case.
