  5. Change "Line" to {Line-2} and click "Save".

  • Your user can use the app as another staff member (account access). Name is an example ("Esther Howard").
  • 1 technicians eligible at this location: active, Role Technician, at least one Department, Location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, Time Clock on. Names are examples ("Esther Howard").
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST Impersonate Start" (used by this case only) with one contact and one asset, and one Approved work order [WO-1] led by [Tech-A]. You (Admin ShopView) lead no work orders at this location.

Setup

  1. Your initials (top right) > Settings > Staff: if no suitable technician exists, click New Staff Member > First Name, Last Name, Email > Role = Technician > Departments = any one (at least one Department is required) > Location = Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 > turn Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record the technician as [Tech-A] (the expected results call this technician "Esther Howard").
  2. Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST Impersonate Start" > Save (the customer page opens). Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name "ZZAUTOTEST", Last Name "Contact" > Save. Assets tab > New Asset > Contact = ZZAUTOTEST Contact > Year 2022 > Make: type "Freight" and pick Freightliner > Model: type "M2" and pick it > Unit "TRK-118" > Save (Contact and Make are required).
  3. Work Orders > Create Work Order > New Work Order: Customer = "ZZAUTOTEST Impersonate Start" > Asset = its asset > Save. If a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create. The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form open. Record the number shown at the top left as [WO-1] (the expected results call it "S1-797").
  4. In New Line > What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service" (it has no parts) > turn Line Approved on > Save & Close.
  5. On [WO-1], on the status card at the left, click Lead Technician and pick [Tech-A]. (Lead Technician is a dropdown only once the work order is Approved; while it is an Estimate it reads "Unassigned" and cannot be changed.) The choice saves at once.
  6. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All > Assigned to me on lists no work orders for you; [WO-1] shows Lead Technician [Tech-A].
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and turn on Assigned to me.
  2. Open Settings > Staff and find [Tech-A].

  4. Wait for the page to finish loading.
  5. Open Work Orders with Assigned to me on.
custom_expected:
Expected results

title: The Sales By Customer Customer filter ticks, selects all and clears
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · a production sign-in for the comparison · about 10 minutes. No test data of its own.
  • Sign in as an Admin (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide; narrower windows show only the List. Your role must see Reports.
  • Work in one location throughout, shown next to the bell in the top bar (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials (top right) > Change Location. Create everything in that location.
  • Before you start: Reports > Sales By Customer; if the Customer filter was changed, set it back to its default.
  • For step 9: a sign-in to production (app.shopview.com) that can see Reports. You only look there; nothing is changed.
custom_steps:
1. Click Reports in the top menu.
  2. In the PERFORMANCE group click "Sales By Customer".
  3. Open the Customer filter. Note that "All customers" is ticked.
  4. Click one option. Write down what happens to the ticks and to the report.
  5. Click the same option again. Write down what happens.
  6. Click the "All customers" box. Write down what happens; if it is already ticked, click it once more and write that down too.
  7. Look for a Clear selection button (write down whether there is one, and its words). If there is one, click it and write down what happens.
  8. Close the filter and set Customer back to "All customers".
  9. In another browser tab sign in to production (app.shopview.com) and repeat steps 1 to 8 on the same report. Compare each step with what you wrote down.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Every step behaves the same on this build as on production (step 9): the same ticks change, the report narrows and widens the same way, and the same buttons are offered.
  • Clicking an option changes which options are ticked, and the report updates to match. (Production today: with "All customers" ticked, clicking an option selects only that option and the button reads "1 selected"; clicking it again goes back to "All customers".)
  • "All customers" ticks every option; clicking it while it is ticked unticks every option. (Production has no separate Clear selection button; clicking the ticked "All customers" box clears the selection.)
  • No error message appears.
  • Mark Failed only if this build behaves differently from production in any step (QA lead's decision below).

Source — where this behaviour comes from

  • Regression for epic SV-10043 (PR #3548); developer's regression list, received 8 Oct 2026, Medium 7; QA handoff test plan (generated 2026-10-08), hotspot 5; PRD Confluence 845185030 (edited 7 Oct 2026) where quoted. Source-verified 8 October 2026.
  • QA lead decision, 12 Oct 2026 (recorded on this test in run 498: https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/tests/view/3792554): this build behaves the same as production, so it passes; an issue that production has too is not a regression.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • Dev reply 7: “The filter option list now supports disabled options. Check that options toggle normally and that Select all and Clear selection work.”

title: Design: The view buttons, filter and search icons look as in the design
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "DC-01-toolbar-tech-view-light-1440.png" and "DC-01-toolbar-board-view-light-1440.png" attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has one Approved work order, {Work-order-1}, led by technician {Technician-A}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590110 Toolbar Icons, {Work-order-1} is S10043-17801 and {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590110 Ana.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "List" shown, "Search" empty, no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On the "Work Orders" page, look at the three buttons of the display switcher.
  2. Look at the icon in "Search" and the icons on "Status", "Assigned to me" and "Asset on Site".
  3. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  4. Look at the density button and the "Column Selection" button.
  5. Look at the icon in "Search" and the filter icons.
  6. Click the density button.
  7. Click "Board View" in the display switcher.
  8. Look at the icon in "Search" and the filter icons.
  9. Click "List" in the display switcher and look at the "Column Selection" button and the other toolbar icons.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: three thin outline icons side by side in a light-grey rounded track (a bulleted list, the head and shoulders of a person, a square board with three bars), the same drawings and size as in the design pictures, drawn in the same slate grey as in the pictures.
  • Step 2: a magnifier in Search; on the filters a circle of short strokes (Status), a clipboard with lines (Assigned to me) and a truck (Asset on Site), thin outlines as in the design picture.
  • Step 3: the Tech View button sits on a white raised segment, the other two look flat, and the switcher icons keep the same slate grey as in List.
  • Step 4: the density button shows three lines with an up-and-down arrow and the Column Selection button a rectangle split into three columns, thin slate outlines as in the Tech View picture.
  • Step 5: the same Search and filter icons as in List at step 2.
  • Step 6: the density menu offers "Compact", "Regular" and "Comfortable", with "Regular" marked as in use.
  • Step 7: the Board View button is now the white raised segment and the switcher icons keep the same slate grey.
  • Step 8: the same Search and filter icons as in List at step 2.
  • Step 9: “List view's column selector button shows the same columns icon as Board View and Tech View, at the same size.” (SV-11668, scope 1) – the same rectangle split into three columns as at step 4. “Only the icon changes. The button's place in the toolbar, its menu and which columns it offers stay as they are.” (SV-11668, scope 2). Apart from that button, the Search and filter icons and the display switcher, List's toolbar icons look as they do in production today.

On 26 Oct 2026 the QA lead asked for this test to follow ticket SV-11668 (Chris Ward, 22 Oct 2026, Ready for Production when read on 26 Oct 2026), which gives List's Column Selection button the same columns icon as Board View and Tech View. It is later than the PRD: PRD version 75 (23 Oct 2026) still says “These are the only changes to List. Every other List icon is unchanged.” (S1-R9a) and “List keeps its existing column chooser exactly as today.” This test takes the ticket as the latest word for the icon only; the button's place, menu and columns still follow the PRD.

Until 15 Oct 2026 the PRD (version 52) left every List icon unchanged, so this case did not judge the filter icons. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 12) that the filter chips and Search use the design file's icons in every display option, List included, and (answer 21) that today's tabs, toolbar and Create Work Order button stay. PRD versions 54 to 71 say so, and this case follows them. The design names the three options Table, By Lead Tech and Board; PRD version 71 still keeps List, Tech View and Board View (answer 24). The Technician filter's wrench icon is checked in the Technician filter design case.

PRD versions 55 and 58 (S1-R9a, S2-R23; Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and PR notes, 15 Oct 2026) add that the display switcher's icons and the toolbar icons are the design's slate colour in every view, List included; steps 1, 3, 4 and 7 check it.

PRD version 71 removes Board View's density button (S3-R11), so this case no longer looks at a density button in Board View; the Board View picture is still used for the switcher and the Search and filter icons.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: Jira ticket SV-11668 “Work Orders List view: column selector icon should match Board View and Tech View” (SV-11668), reported by Chris Ward on 22 Oct 2026, description read 26 Oct 2026

  • Scope 1: “List view's column selector button shows the same columns icon as Board View and Tech View, at the same size.”
  • Scope 2: “Only the icon changes. The button's place in the toolbar, its menu and which columns it offers stay as they are.”
  • Scope 3: “Board View and Tech View are unchanged.”

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 71 (20 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, stories SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options) and SV-10049 (Story 6, Density in Tech View and Board View); ticket SV-11319

  • S1-R9a: “The switcher uses the design’s icons at 20px: List is Lucide `list`, Tech View is `user-round`, Board View is `square-kanban`. In Tech View and Board View these icons are the design’s: density (`row-height` in Tech View, `card-height` in Board View, custom icons in the design system’s icon set), collapse chevron (`chevron-down`), pin and unpin (`pin` / `pin-off`), Invoiced or Paid lock (`lock`), Unassigned avatar (`user-round`) and the empty state when there are no work orders at all (`clipboard-list`). The filtered no-results state is the List’s, magnifier included (S1-N1). The filter chips and Search use the design file’s icons in every display option, List included, each exactly as the design file draws it. The display switcher (new on every view, List included) shows the design’s slate icons in every view, so it keeps one color as the user moves between views. These are the only changes to List. Every other List icon is unchanged.”
  • S2-R23: “In Tech View and Board View, as in the design: a technician avatar without a photo is a light-grey circle (--sv-grey-100, #EEF2F6) with initials in --sv-grey-600 (#4B5565) in light mode, which meets accessible contrast (6.7:1; the design file’s #697586 is 4.2:1); dark mode uses the design’s dark colors; group and column header names are 14px, weight 600, in the design’s slate text color (#364152), with the design’s smaller initials, in the same --sv-grey-600 (#4B5565) as every other avatar’s initials; Board card customer and total price are weight 500; toolbar and switcher icons are the design’s slate color (the switcher in List too, S1-R9a). Technician avatars, and the Service Advisor avatar, follow density in Tech View as in the design: 20px, 24px and 32px on rows and 24px, 28px and 36px on group headers at Compact, Regular and Comfortable; Board View card avatars stay 24px. The Progress bar is 48 by 4px at Compact, as in the design. The name bubble on hover over a technician avatar on a row or card (the +N included) opens above the avatar, in both views; group and column header avatars keep the browser’s plain name tip, because the name is printed beside them. In Tech View, Status, Waiting On Parts and Progress are left-aligned. The Density and Columns tooltips open above their button, like the switcher’s (S1-R9b), and are hidden while their menu is open. List is unchanged.”
  • S1-R9: “The switcher visually indicates the active display option.”
  • S6-R1: “Offer Compact, Regular, and Comfortable density in Tech View. Board View has no Density control in this release (S3-R11).”
  • Goals: “List remains the default and is unchanged from production. The only changes to the Work Orders page are the display switcher and the icons on the filter chips and Search, which follow the design file in every display option, List included (S1-R9a). Today’s tabs, toolbar layout and Create Work Order button stay as they are.”

From: Chris Ward's answers 12, 21 and 24, "WO Board and Tech View – questions for Chris Ward (14 Oct 2026)" (Google Sheet 1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU, tab "Questions for Chris"), answered 15 Oct 2026, read 15 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 12: “12. Changed ruling: the filter chips and Search use the design file's icons in every display option, List included, each exactly as the design file draws it. This is the only change to List. New wording in Goals and S1-R9a.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 21: “21. (a). Today's tabs, toolbar and Create Work Order button stay. The only changes to the page are the switcher and the chip and Search icons (Q12).”
  • Chris Ward's answer 24: “24. (a). The tooltips read List, Tech View and Board View. S1-R9b.”

  • Step 11: the menu opens.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) Phase 11. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 28, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Until 15 Oct 2026 Story 11 only listed keyboard behaviour the design still had to define, so this case asked the tester to try keys and write down what each did. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 28): Tab reaches every control, Enter opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the control that opened a menu or dialog, reassigning by keyboard goes through the ⋯ menu, and there is no keyboard drag. PRD version 54 rewrites Story 11 into these requirements, and this case now checks them.

Chris Ward's answer 28 (15 Oct 2026) and PRD version 54 said Tab reaches every row, card and header in on-screen order. PRD versions 55, 60 and 61 (15 and 16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and the QA triage of SV-11395, SV-11397, SV-11422 and SV-11421) changed this: each view is one Tab stop that lands on a work order, and the arrow keys move between cards, rows, headers and columns. Version 62 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling on Bilal's QA questions 32 and 33) added where the first Tab lands when nothing has been focused yet, and version 67 (19 Oct 2026) reworded S11-R9 for the Assign or Reassign lead technician dialog. In versions 66 to 68 the messages after a lead change became "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}" and "{work order number} moved to Unassigned", with Undo. This case follows version 68, the latest.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S11-R1: “Each view is a single Tab stop. Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or, when none has been, the first work order shown in on-screen order: the first row or card in Unassigned, or the first technician’s first row or card when Unassigned is collapsed or empty (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
  • S11-R9: “Assigning, reassigning and unassigning by keyboard go through the more-actions menu: Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician (S3-R14) opens the lead technician dialog, and Unassign is a menu item. There is no keyboard drag in this release, so reordering work orders and technicians is by mouse or touch only.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • Tech plan Phase 11 dialog: “The dialog is the keyboard path for moving work between technicians; it runs the same permission and status checks as the pointer path (S11-N1)”

Count every eligible technician at the location (Settings > Staff) and record the number as [Tech-count] (the expected results give "8" as the example).

Setup

  2. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm each technician below is active at this location with Time Clock on, or add it: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as "Esther Howard" (keep this name, the expected results use it); at least seven more (e.g. Ralph Edwards, Jenny Wilson, Kristin Watson, Theresa Webb, Dana Ortiz, Brenda Martinez, Cameron Williamson).
  3. Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Column Scroll" > Save (if it already exists, open it instead). On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, TRK-118) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  4. Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Column Scroll" and its asset > Save. The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form open: in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; the build offers only ready-made lines), turn Line Approved on > Save & Close; the work order becomes Approved. Repeat for about 25 + 20 + one per other technician (numbers on this site look like "S10043-17581").
  5. Set the leads: on an Approved work order pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned. Here: about 25 with no lead; about 20 = Esther Howard; one or more each for the other technicians.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S3-E1, read 8 Oct 2026; S3-E2 re-read at version 65 on 19 Oct 2026. Review Decisions 853901313 UX-11 / DR-40. PRD inline comment Branko Cicovic 28 Sep 2026 (only content inside the columns scrolls).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-E2 (version 65): “Allow horizontal scrolling when technician columns exceed the available viewport; never hide technicians automatically. The board’s sideways scrollbar is 16px thick, and its grab handle is never shorter than 150px at any screen width or number of technician columns. When more of the board fits on screen, the handle is longer, as the browser draws it. The scrollbars inside each column are unchanged. title: SV-11524 - Work orders of a deleted lead sit under Deleted technician, which takes no drops
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two technicians are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role: {Technician-A} and {Technician-B}. {Technician-A} was made for this case only and has no labor on any work order, because this test deletes that staff record.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C614711 Dana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C614711 Eli.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has two Approved work orders: {Work-order-1} led by {Technician-A}, and {Work-order-2} with no lead technician. {Technician-B} is not the technician on any line of {Work-order-1}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C614711 Deleted Lead, and {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are S10043-17901 and S10043-17902.
  • Starting screen: your initials (top right) > "Settings" > "Staff", in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the pencil icon on {Technician-A}.
  2. Click "Delete" and confirm.
  3. Go to "Work Orders" > "All" > "Board View".
  4. Type the name of {Customer-A} in "Search".
  5. Read the header of the column that holds the card for {Work-order-1}.
  6. Drag the card for {Work-order-2} from "Unassigned" onto that column and let go.
  7. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  8. Click "List" in the display switcher.
  9. Click "Board View" in the display switcher.
  10. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the staff record of {Technician-A} opens.
  • Step 2: {Technician-A} is no longer in the "Staff" list.
  • Step 3: Board View shows.
  • Step 4: the cards for {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} show.
  • Step 5: the header reads "Deleted technician", shows the inactive marker and has no drag grip.
  • Step 6: the drop is refused: the card for {Work-order-2} stays in "Unassigned".
  • Step 7: {Work-order-1} sits in a group headed "Deleted technician" with the inactive marker.
  • Step 8: in the row for {Work-order-1} the "Lead Technician" cell reads "Unassigned", as List shows today.
  • Step 9: Board View shows again.
  • Step 10: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with an "Undo" button.

Step 8 expects "Unassigned": PRD version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling) changed S3-R20e to say so (it said "blank, as today"), as the QA lead decided on 19 Oct 2026.

Known problem (SV-11416, open: https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11416): today, at step 5, the column reads "Unknown Technician" with a generic person icon, no inactive marker and a drag grip, and the deleted technician's name is not shown.

1. If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new.

2. If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it.

3. If it passes, the fix has shipped: tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S3-R20e, S4-N5, S3-N4, S2-N3 and S4-R5, read 19 Oct 2026. Defect SV-11416 (open). Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

SV-11416 asked the product owner what happens when a lead technician is deleted; the spec covered only a deactivated lead. PRD version 59 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling on Slavcho Mitrov's question on SV-11416) added S3-R20e: such work orders sit under "Deleted technician" with the inactive marker and no grip, take no drops, can be dragged out, and List shows the lead blank (version 68 changed this to "Unassigned"). In versions 66 to 68 (19 Oct 2026) the message after a lead change became "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo (step 10). This case follows version 59 and later (was: no "Unknown Technician" column, the header naming the technician as List does).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R20e: “Work orders whose lead technician was deleted in Settings → Staff (the name no longer exists) sit in one column on Board View and one group in Tech View labeled “Deleted technician”, with the inactive marker and no drag grip. Work orders can be dragged out of it; nothing can be dropped onto it. List shows “Unassigned” in the Lead Technician column for these work orders, as today.”
  • S4-N5: “Nothing can be dropped onto the column/group of an inactive technician (S2-N2, S3-N2) or of a technician who is not enrolled at this location (S3-R20c).”
  • S3-N4: “Show an inactive indicator on deactivated technician columns.”
  • S2-N3: “Indicate deactivated technicians as inactive in group headers.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”

title: Invoiced and Paid work orders show why the lead can't be changed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 25 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • [Tech-A]: one eligible technician at this location. A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • [Tech-B]: a second eligible technician at this location (same rules as [Tech-A]). Their column shows on Board View and their group in Tech View even with no work orders, so the locked work orders can be dragged over it.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" (used by this case only), with a contact, and two work orders with Lead Technician [Tech-A] set before invoicing: [WO-1] Invoiced and [WO-2] Paid.
  • Names and numbers are examples; what must hold: one Invoiced and one Paid work order, both with a lead.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard) and [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. How to reach each status (standard steps): Estimate = a new work order whose lines are not approved. Approved = approve its lines. In Progress = a technician clicks Start time clock on an approved line's Labor row. Review = set the work order to Ready for Review with its status control. Complete = enter a tech story on every line, complete each line, then complete the work order. Invoiced = Finance tab > Create Invoice (the work order needs a contact person). Paid = record a full payment on that invoice. Declined = decline the estimate.
  6. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Assign lead technician > click the technician; it is assigned at once.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-511): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Invoiced.
    • [WO-2] (e.g. S1-366): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Paid.
  7. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" shows [WO-1] (Invoiced) and [WO-2] (Paid), both led by [Tech-A]. If not, fix the status or lead before starting; then clear the search.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" in Search.
  3. Look at the [WO-1] card and write down any sign that it can only be reordered within its technician (e.g. a lock icon).
  4. Hover the lock icon on the [WO-1] card and read its tooltip.
  5. Hover the card, click More actions and hover the Reassign lead technician action.
  6. Read the tooltip shown next to the Reassign lead technician action.
  7. Hover the Unassign action and read its tooltip.
  8. Press Escape to close the menu.
  9. Drag the [WO-1] card over [Tech-B]'s column and, without releasing it, read the note at the top of [Tech-B]'s column.
  10. Release the card and read which column it is in.
  11. Repeat steps 3 to 10 for [WO-2].
  12. Repeat steps 3 to 11 in Tech View on the rows, dragging each row over [Tech-B]'s group.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Invoiced and Paid cards and rows carry a lock icon, the visible sign that they can only be reordered within their current technician and not moved to another one.
  • Hovering the lock icon shows the tooltip “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-1] and “Paid · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-2].
  • Reassign lead technician and Unassign are shown disabled, and their tooltip reads exactly: Invoiced · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-1]) or Paid · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-2]). (A straight or curly apostrophe is not a difference.)
  • While [WO-1] or [WO-2] is dragged over [Tech-B]'s column or group, the note at its top reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-1]) or “Paid · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-2]).
  • On release the drop is refused: the card or row stays with [Tech-A], and its lead stays [Tech-A].

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-N6, S4-N7 and S4-N2, read 19 Oct 2026. PRD §9 User Feedback Summary row "Reassignment not allowed in current status". Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): lock icon next to the number with tooltip "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" and a locked menu note; since PRD version 68 the PRD uses the same words, and the PRD text is asserted here. Source-verified 19 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S4-N7: “Visually indicate that an Invoiced or Paid work order can only be reordered within its current technician, not moved to another one.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Invoiced or Paid status. An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Declined and Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today.”

title: The keyboard cannot get around permission or status limits
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • A second user {User-B} has the custom role {Role-A}, which allows Work orders: View only, and is signed in in a second browser.
    For example: {User-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C97020 Viewer and {Role-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C97020 View Only.
  • Technician {Technician-A} is active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and is pinned in Board View for both users.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C97020 Ana.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has two work orders led by {Technician-A}: {Work-order-1}, Approved, and {Work-order-2}, Invoiced. None has a shift on the Schedule.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C97020 Limits, and {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are S10043-17711 and S10043-17712.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide, for both users.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. In the second browser (signed in as {User-B}), click once in the "Search" box.
  2. Press Tab until a card shows a focus ring.
  3. Use the arrow keys to move the focus ring to the card for {Work-order-1}.
  4. Press Tab.
  5. Press Enter.
  6. Press Space, then Shift with each arrow key.
  7. In your own browser ("Admin" role), click once in the "Search" box.
  8. Press Tab until a card shows a focus ring.
  9. Use the arrow keys to move the focus ring to the card for {Work-order-2}.
  10. Press Tab.
  11. Press Enter.
  12. Choose "Reassign lead technician" with the arrow keys and press Enter.
  13. Press Escape.
  14. Press Space, then Shift with each arrow key.
  15. Refresh the page.
  16. Click the card for {Work-order-2}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the cursor is in the "Search" box.
  • Step 2: a card shows the focus ring.
  • Step 3: the card for {Work-order-1} shows the focus ring.
  • Step 4: if the card has a "More actions" (…) button, it now has the focus; otherwise focus leaves the board.
  • Step 5: "Reassign lead technician" and "Unassign" cannot be reached: no menu opens, or they are not offered, or they are disabled and nothing happens.
  • Step 6: no key moves {Work-order-1}; it keeps its place and its lead, {Technician-A}.
  • Step 7: the cursor is in the "Search" box.
  • Step 8: a card shows the focus ring.
  • Step 9: the card for {Work-order-2} shows the focus ring.
  • Step 10: the card's "More actions" (…) button shows and has the focus.
  • Step 11: the menu opens and "Reassign lead technician" and "Unassign" are disabled, with the note "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned".
  • Step 12: nothing happens; no dialog opens.
  • Step 13: the menu closes.
  • Step 14: no key moves {Work-order-2} to another technician.
  • Step 15: Board View shows {Work-order-2} in {Technician-A}'s column.
  • Step 16: the work order page opens and "Lead Technician" reads {Technician-A}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10054 (Story 11, Keyboard access and focus), SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S11-N1, S11-R9, S4-N1, S4-N6, S11-R1 and S11-R3, read 19 Oct 2026. Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) Phase 11. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 28, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Until 15 Oct 2026 Story 11 only listed keyboard behaviour the design still had to define, so this case asked the tester to try keys and write down what each did. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 28): Tab reaches every control, Enter opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the control that opened a menu or dialog, reassigning by keyboard goes through the ⋯ menu, and there is no keyboard drag. PRD version 54 rewrites Story 11 into these requirements, and this case now checks them.

Chris Ward's answer 28 (15 Oct 2026) and PRD version 54 said Tab reaches every row, card and header in on-screen order. PRD versions 55, 60 and 61 (15 and 16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and the QA triage of SV-11395, SV-11397, SV-11422 and SV-11421) changed this: each view is one Tab stop that lands on a work order, and the arrow keys move between cards, rows, headers and columns. PRD version 62 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward) added where the first Tab lands when nothing has been focused yet (the first row or card in Unassigned, or the first technician’s first one when Unassigned is collapsed or empty); the steps are unchanged. This case follows version 68, the latest.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S11-N1: “Keyboard access must not bypass action permissions or work order status restrictions.”
  • S11-R9: “Assigning, reassigning and unassigning by keyboard go through the more-actions menu: Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician (S3-R14) opens the lead technician dialog, and Unassign is a menu item. There is no keyboard drag in this release, so reordering work orders and technicians is by mouse or touch only.”
  • S4-N1: “Require Work Orders create and edit permission to drag work orders or use Assign lead technician, Reassign lead technician or Unassign. A user without it who drags a card or row over another technician’s column or group sees the design’s note “You don’t have permission to assign technicians” at the top of that column or group, and the drop is refused.”
  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S11-R1: “Each view is a single Tab stop. Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or, when none has been, the first work order shown in on-screen order: the first row or card in Unassigned, or the first technician’s first row or card when Unassigned is collapsed or empty (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
  • Tech plan Phase 11 tests: “a keyboard-initiated reassign is refused for a locked status and without permission (S11-N1).”

custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Hover {Work-order-1}'s card in {Technician-A}'s column and click its More actions (…) button.
  4. Click Reassign lead technician.
  5. Read every row in the dialog, from the top.
  6. Click {Technician-B}'s row.
  7. If a "Clear … scheduled shifts?" question opens, click Keep shifts.
  8. Hover the card, now in {Technician-B}'s column, and click its More actions (…) button.
  9. Click Unassign.
  10. If a "Clear … scheduled shifts?" question opens, click Keep shifts.
  11. Hover the card, now in the Unassigned column, click its More actions (…) button and click Assign lead technician.
  12. Type the first letters of {Technician-C}'s name in the dialog's search box, then click Cancel.
  13. Click the card to open the work order and read Lead Technician.
  14. Press the browser Back button and click Tech View in the display switcher.
  15. Hover {Work-order-1}'s row in the Unassigned group, click its More actions (…) button and click Assign lead technician.
  16. Read every row in the dialog, from the top.
  17. Click {Technician-A}'s row.
  18. If a "Clear … scheduled shifts?" question opens, click Keep shifts.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the dialog opens with the title "Reassign lead technician".
  • Step 5: the dialog has a Search technicians box, then one list with no grouping of the eligible technicians of {Location-A}, {Technician-A}, {Technician-B} and {Technician-C}, each with an avatar and an "N open" count. There is no Unassigned row. {User-B}, {Technician-D} and {Technician-E} are not listed. The only button is Cancel.
  • Step 6: the dialog closes at once, with no other click, and the card moves to {Technician-B}'s column. The message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with an Undo button.
  • Step 9: the card moves to the Unassigned column and the message "{Work-order-1} moved to Unassigned" shows, with an Undo button.
  • Step 11: the menu offers "Assign lead technician" (not "Reassign lead technician"), and the dialog opens with the title "Assign lead technician".
  • Step 12: the dialog closes and nothing changes: the card stays in the Unassigned column.
  • Step 13: the work order page shows no lead technician.
  • Step 16: the Tech View dialog, titled "Assign lead technician", shows the same technicians as at step 5, with no Unassigned row.
  • Step 17: the dialog closes at once and the row moves to {Technician-A}'s group. The message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-A}" shows, with an Undo button.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S3-R14, S4-R4, S4-R12, S4-R13, S4-R14 and S4-R5, read 19 Oct 2026. Eligibility from PRD section 5 Terminology (Technician) and S2-R7. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 19, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 19) that the dialog is final as drawn (search, avatars, N open per technician, no grouping) with Unassigned as its first row, and PRD version 54 said so. PRD version 66 (19 Oct 2026, after SV-11522 and SV-11524) took Unassigned out of the dialog, made a click on a technician assign at once, and named the menu item and the dialog "Assign lead technician" or "Reassign lead technician"; removing the lead is the menu's Unassign action. This case follows PRD version 68, which is later.

Known problem (SV-11522 and SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the More actions menu on a work order with no lead says "Reassign lead technician"; the lead technician dialog lists "Unassigned" at the top, and choosing a technician needs a click on a "Reassign" button; the message after a lead change reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R14: “Include the lead technician action in the card’s more-actions menu: “Assign lead technician” on a work order with no lead technician, “Reassign lead technician” on one that has a lead technician.”
  • S4-R4: “The card or row more-actions menu opens the lead technician dialog, titled “Assign lead technician” or “Reassign lead technician” to match the menu item it was opened from (S3-R14).”
  • S4-R12: “The dialog offers eligible active technicians in the current location and nothing else. Unassigned is not offered there: Unassigned is the place for work orders without a lead, not a technician, and removing the lead is the menu’s Unassign action (S11-R9) or a drag to Unassigned. It follows the design: a Search technicians box, each technician with their avatar and N open count, no grouping.”
  • S4-R13: “Clicking a technician in the dialog assigns them at once; there is no confirm button, and the dialog’s only button is Cancel. When the shift-clearing prompt applies (S4-R28) it shows first, and the change is made from the prompt. Clicking the work order’s current lead closes the dialog with no change (S4-N4).”
  • S4-R14: “Canceling the dialog leaves the lead unchanged.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”

title: Dragging to another technician changes the lead, Unassigned clears it
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 20 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • Technicians (examples, the expected results call them by first name or full name): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo", "ZZAUTOTEST Cal Charlie". A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > the staff member's edit icon > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customers (used by this case only, each with one contact and one asset): "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change Golf Co". The steps and expected results call them by the end of the name ("Alpha Co", "Golf Co").
  • Work orders (all Approved): lead Ana — Alpha Co; no lead — Golf Co.
  • None of these technicians has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders (check the Schedule page). If a window titled "Clear … scheduled shifts?" still appears during a move, click "Keep shifts".

Setup

  1. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo", "ZZAUTOTEST Cal Charlie" exist and count as technicians at this location (edit icon > Edit Staff Member). To add one: New Staff Member with those settings (at least one Department is required) (e.g. first name "ZZAUTOTEST Ana", last name "Alpha") > Save & Close.
  2. Create this case's customers: "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change Golf Co". For each: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name > Save; on the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact); then the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  3. Create each work order listed in the Preconditions: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Move it to the status named: a new work order starts as Estimate (it opens with the New Line form: pick a ready-made line and Save & Close); for Approved turn on Line Approved on its line; for In Progress click Start on the line's Labor row (stop the clock afterwards with Stop > Clock Out); for Review click the line's Complete button, type a Tech Story (fill any missing detail it asks for, e.g. Mileage) and click Complete Line (the List shows "Ready For Review"); for Complete then click Mark Reviewed, enter the VIN if asked and click Confirm Review; for Declined save the line with Line Approved off and click Decline on it (it must be the work order's only line); for Invoiced complete and review it first, then Finance tab > Create Invoice; for Paid, after invoicing, Finance tab > New Payment for the full amount > Make Payment. Set the lead technician before invoicing. Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page (leave it as Unassigned for an unassigned one). (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801); the steps call each work order by the end of its customer name (e.g. "Alpha Co").
  4. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > List > type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change" in Search — exactly 2 work orders show, both Approved: Alpha Co led by Ana, Golf Co with no lead (Unassigned). On the Schedule neither has a shift. If anything differs, correct that work order (status or Lead Technician) before starting.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change" in Search so only this case's work orders show.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher (tooltip "Board View").
  4. Drag the Alpha Co card from Ana's column into Ben's column and release.
  5. Click the Alpha Co card to open the work order and read its Lead Technician, then go back with the browser Back button.
  6. Drag the Alpha Co card from Ben's column into the Unassigned column and release.
  7. Open the Alpha Co work order again, read Lead Technician, then go back.
  8. Drag the Golf Co card from the Unassigned column into Cal's column and release.
  9. Open the Golf Co work order, read Lead Technician, then go back.
  10. Click Tech View in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar (tooltip "Tech View").
  11. Drag the Golf Co row from Cal's group into Ana's group and release, then open it and read Lead Technician.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • After step 4 the card sits in Ben's column and a message naming the work order and Ben appears, with an Undo button (e.g. "S1-801 assigned to ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo", with Alpha Co's own number). It closes by itself after about 5 seconds while the pointer is not over it.
  • Step 5: the work order page shows Lead Technician Ben Bravo.
  • After step 6 the card sits in Unassigned and the message "<Alpha Co's number> moved to Unassigned" appears (e.g. "S1-801 moved to Unassigned"), with an Undo button.
  • Step 7: the work order page shows no lead technician.
  • Steps 8 and 9: the Golf Co card moved into Cal's column and its work order page shows Lead Technician Cal Charlie.

title: Undo puts each line back to the technician it had; an empty line stays empty
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 20 minutes.
  • Build: the QA branch for the Undo fast follow, sv11567 (https://sv11567.qa.shopview.com).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • Two eligible technicians at this location: [Tech-A] "Ralph Edwards" and [Tech-B] "Dana Ortiz". A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" (used by this case only) with one work order [WO-1], created on this build, Approved, no lead technician, with three lines: Line 1 Unassigned (no technician) · Line 2 Explicit (its own technician [Tech-B]) · Line 3 Complete (no technician, status Complete).
  • The technician names are used in the expected results and stay as written; the line names are only labels and the number is an example.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] = "Ralph Edwards" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it), [Tech-B] = "Dana Ortiz" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Line names in this case (such as "Line 1") are only labels for you: the New Line form's "What Are You Doing?" box only offers ready-made lines (typed text finds no results), so pick any ready-made line for each one (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot") and write down which is which.
  6. Create a new work order on this build for "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" with no lead technician: Work Orders > Create Work Order > pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Record its number as [WO-1] (e.g. "S1-710").
    • Add "Line 1 Unassigned" with no technician.
    • Add "Line 2 Explicit" and in Edit Line set Technicians = [Tech-B].
    • Add "Line 3 Complete" with no technician, approve it, enter a tech story and complete it.
    • Approve the other lines (the work order reads Approved).
    • Write down each line's Labor row: Line 1 Unassigned, Line 2 [Tech-B], Line 3 Unassigned (Complete).
  7. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" shows [WO-1] in the Unassigned column (Board View) with status Approved; its Lines tab matches what you wrote down. If not, fix the line or create a fresh work order before starting; then clear the search.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST FF Undo Lines" in Search.
  3. Drag the [WO-1] card from the Unassigned column onto Ralph Edwards' column and let go.
  4. Before the message closes (about 5 seconds), click "Undo" on the message.
  5. Click the [WO-1] card to open the work order, open the Lines tab and read each line's Labor row.
  6. Go back to Work Orders (Board View, the same search) and drag the [WO-1] card from Unassigned onto Ralph Edwards' column again. This time do not click Undo.
  7. Open [WO-1] again, open the Lines tab and read each line's Labor row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

The PRD rule this test checks, word for word (S4-R32): “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Each labor line goes back to the technician it had before the change, and a line that had none goes back to none; Undo does not apply the S4-R8 line rules. Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt. After Undo the design’s toast reads “Assignment undone”, with no Undo button on it. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Move the work order back by hand.” shows.”

  • Step 3: the card moves to Ralph Edwards' column and the message "[WO-1] assigned to Ralph Edwards" shows (e.g. "S1-710 assigned to Ralph Edwards"), with "Undo".
  • Step 4: the message closes, the card goes back to the Unassigned column and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button.
  • Step 5: the lines are exactly as before the change: Line 1 reads Unassigned (no technician), Line 2 still shows Dana Ortiz, Line 3 (Complete) still reads Unassigned.
  • Step 7: Line 1 now shows Ralph Edwards, Line 2 still shows Dana Ortiz, Line 3 still reads Unassigned. This shows the lead change does move Line 1, so step 5 proves Undo put it back.

A field picked while Compact is on shows on the card once the user switches to Detailed.” “Crew avatars show without the see financial data permission; only the total needs it (S5-E2).”

  • Step 1: "Card size" sits beside "Column Selection" between the toolbar's two dividers. There is no "Density" control on Board View.

  • Step 3: the card keeps only the rank, work order number, status badge, assign button, customer and asset. The hours, created date, progress bar, details row (Service Advisor, Line Count), crew avatars and total are hidden. Card padding is 10px top and bottom and 12px left and right, and the gap between blocks is 6px. The columns, their order and the order of the cards are the same as before.
  • Step 4: "Column Selection" offers the same fields as in Detailed. The card stays Compact: Created Date does not show on it.

Card padding is 12px and the gap between blocks is 8px.
